meaning.verdict: PASS = may change the live paper system; FAIL = nothing changes; the lesson is kept

reviews.title: Explorer scorecard: entries, warning bells, weakest setup
reviews.forwarded_because: The 7-year Explorer replay lost money after costs. Three things looked suspicious: limit orders that never filled seemed to do better, the warning-bell exits seemed to cut winners, and setup E5 was the worst.
reviews.question: Do market entries, no warning bells, or dropping E5 make the Explorer better on data it was not tuned on?
reviews.result: No change passed. Market entries were clearly worse. The 'missed orders did better' evidence was hindsight bias (our error). Bells neither help nor hurt normally but save money in crashes, so they stay. E5 is the weakest setup but not by enough to drop.
reviews.changed: Nothing in the live rules. Scorecard wording corrected; the chase shadow no longer counts as evidence about entries.

reviews.title: Learning from other traders (Hyperliquid, 65 accounts)
reviews.forwarded_because: Our own setups showed no edge, so we checked where real traders entered and whether their timing carries information our rules miss.
reviews.question: Is there usable information in when real traders buy, and does their skill persist?
reviews.result: Their entry timing carried almost no information (a tiny 1-hour edge) and skill did not persist from one period to the next. One pattern stood out: they did better buying weakness than strength. That became review #3.
reviews.changed: Nothing live. Traders stay reference only, never teachers.

reviews.title: Buying weakness (dip setups E6-E8)
reviews.forwarded_because: Review #2 found traders did better buying dips.
reviews.question: Do dip entries beat random entries and pay NDAX costs on 2017-2023 data?
reviews.result: Buying when 15m RSI is under 30 beat random entries (first rule ever to beat chance on unseen data) but by far too little to pay fees and spread. Every variant lost after costs.
reviews.changed: Dip setups E6-E8 are watched only (sightings for the atlas), never traded.

reviews.title: Portfolio trend layer (T3) vs buy-and-hold
reviews.forwarded_because: Reviews #1-#3 showed the only consistent return is being in the market during multi-week uptrends, and the only consistent protection is getting out in slow crashes.
reviews.question: Can a simple daily trend rule (hold a coin above its 50- and 20-day averages while BTC is above its 50-day) beat buy-and-hold with less pain?
reviews.result: T3 passed: +13% vs buy-and-hold -22% in 2024-26 with about half the drawdown, and it sat out most crashes. Weak spot: it fails if fees double, so it must trade rarely.
reviews.changed: T3 runs as the portfolio layer (MAIN book you approve, SHADOW book always automatic) since 2026-09-30.
